finding.title: metrics.stats (and call_logs.model_alias) keyed by the unresolved, length-unbounded client model string -> permanent unbounded growth
finding.impact: One leaked gateway API key + a loop of `POST /v1/chat/completions {"model":"x-<counter>","messages":[]}` (each answered 404 in microseconds, unthrottled because the limiter runs later) permanently grows `mt.stats` by one 960-byte ModelStat plus an attacker-length string key per request; nothing is ever evicted, so the footprint is a monotonic high-water mark for the life of the process. Retention is amplified 3 ways: (a) every /metrics scrape re-serializes every key (see dos-2), (b) every such request also writes a call_logs row carrying the full raw string in an indexed column, so the SQLite file and its index grow at attacker-chosen rate and size, and (c) the same map is iterated by the admin /status page. Net effect is a slow, irreversible memory + disk exhaustion path that ends in OOM or a full-query collapse, and it cannot be mitigated by configuration because no bound exists on key count or key length.
finding.recommendation: Three changes: (1) validate the client model string at parse time (reject >128 bytes / non `[A-Za-z0-9._:/\[\]-]`) in adapter.ParseRequest so no downstream consumer ever sees an unbounded token; (2) move `s.mx.Observe(...)` out of the pre-resolution defer and call it only after resolution, using the resolved alias, or bucket unresolved names into a single fixed key such as "__unknown__"; (3) bound the map: cap `len(mt.stats)` (e.g. 1024, evict/merge overflow into "__other__") and drop entries whose `lastSec` is >60s stale in the existing QPS() sweep (they already report 0 QPS, so eviction is loss-free). Truncate ModelAlias to 64 bytes before writeLog.
finding.mitigations_checked: 16 MiB inbound body cap (gateway.go:322) bounds one key's size per request but not the count; gateway auth is required (gateway.go:215-221), so the attacker needs one valid API key; MaxConnections (gateway.go:195) limits concurrency, not the cumulative key set; ErrorEvent ring IS bounded (metrics.go:77-79 `if len(mt.recent) > 50 {`); slb.rr cursors ARE pruned (slb.go:213-217) - no equivalent for stats; the guard/quota/rate-limit steps do not run on this path, so they provide no protection.

reason:
CONFIRMED at high. Every load-bearing quote was verified verbatim at the cited line numbers after reading metrics.go (124 lines), prom.go (154), gateway.go (831), adapter.go parse paths, model.go:246-268, audit.go (124), routes.go, prom.go(admin collector), dashboard.go and main.go end-to-end. The chain is intact and I found no mitigation anywhere in the flow.

(1) The unbounded insert is real and permanent. metrics.go:56-71 is the quoted block verbatim (line 60 `s := mt.stats[model]`, 61 `if s == nil {`, 62 `s = &ModelStat{lastSec: now}`, 63 `mt.stats[model] = s`, 64 `}`). A whole-file read confirms the ONLY writers of mt.stats are New() (line 53) and line 63; there is no delete, no size cap, no TTL, no reset on hot reload. Repo-wide grep for `delete\(|mt\.stats|\.stats\[` returned 6 hits, none of them an eviction in metrics.go -> the filed '0 hits for delete(mt.stats' is accurate. QPS() (88-103) rotates each stat and copies out but never prunes, so the filed recommendation to evict >60s-stale keys there is sound: such entries already render QPS 0 (line 99), making eviction loss-free.

(2) The retained key really is the raw, unresolved client string. Handle registers the observation defer at gateway.go:314 (`defer func() {`) and calls `s.mx.Observe(ap.alias, ap.status != "ok")` at line 318 — deferred, so it fires on every early return. `ap.alias = cr.Model` at 334 (raw) precedes resolution at 335 (`ups, ok := snap.Aliases[cr.Model]`), the context-suffix retry at 339-346 and the implicit-upstream retry at 351-354. The only place ap.alias is overwritten with a resolved value is line 343, inside the strip branch, which by construction means the name resolved. So the rejection path at 356-361 (`ap.errMsg = "unknown model alias: " + cr.Model` / clientError 404 / `return`) observes the attacker's literal string. Note the same raw string is also duplicated into ErrorMsg at 357 and echoed verbatim in the 404 body at 359.

(3) Ordering / absence of throttling verified. The 404 returns at 356-361, strictly before the API-key model allowlist at 370 (`if !apiKey.AllowsModel(cr.Model) {`), the guard step (381-407), the rate limiter at 410 (`if ok2, hit := s.rl.Allow(snap, apiKey.ID, ap.alias); !ok2 {`) and quota at 419. Consequence: a key explicitly restricted to a single model can still mint arbitrary stats keys, and no per-key counter is consulted or incremented on this path. There is no global limiter either: AuthMiddleware (189-231) only enforces MaxConnections (195, concurrency not cumulative), key validity (215-221) and IP allowlist (222-227); main.go mounts only gin.Recovery, security headers and an access logger (95-118). TRUSTED_PROXIES/MaxConnections therefore provide nothing here, as filed.

(4) No length/charset bound anywhere in the parse path. adapter.go checks only emptiness on all three protocols: 120-121 (chat), 212-213 (responses), 316-317 (anthropic). Combined with the 16 MiB `io.LimitReader(c.Request.Body, 16<<20)` at gateway.go:322, a single retained map key can be ~16 MiB, permanently.

(5) Persistence and re-emission verified. gateway.go:273 `Protocol: p.proto, ModelAlias: p.alias, ...`; model.go:253 `ModelAlias string `gorm:"size:64;index" json:"model_alias"` (and ErrorMsg size:512 at 266). Those are GORM schema declarations only — on the default SQLite engine there is no length enforcement and no truncation anywhere in the write flow (audit.go:37-47 Write -> writerLoop -> CreateInBatches at 67). Call audit is on by default (settings.go:33 `CallAuditEnabled: true`) and non-ok statuses bypass the only-errors/sampling filters (gateway.go:257-259), so every 404 does insert a row. prom.go:135-139 emits the retained string twice per key (`l := `model="` + promEsc(q.Model) + `"` at 136; used at 137 and 138), and writeMetric (48-58) reprints HELP+TYPE per sample -> 6 lines per key per scrape; /metrics itself is deliberately unauthenticated (routes.go:19-24 comment 'no JWT by design').

(6) Additional verified consequence that STRENGTHENS the finding (not speculation, and not the already-known dos-2 scrape-cost point): the growth converts into an unauthenticated stall of authenticated traffic. Observe takes mt.mu for its whole body (metrics.go:58-59, unlock deferred at 59); QPS() holds the same mutex across the full map iteration (89-100); and the unauthenticated /metrics handler reaches QPS() via admin/prom.go:15 (`snap.ModelQPS = s.mx.QPS()`) while holding promMu (prom.go:113). Once an attacker has minted N entries with one gateway key, any unauthenticated client polling /metrics forces an O(N) scan that blocks every gateway request in its deferred Observe at line 318. So the attacker-chosen N is also a persistent, restart-only amplifier of unauthenticated gateway-wide latency and of /metrics response size. The same map is likewise iterated for the authenticated admin view at dashboard.go:137 (`"qps_by_model": s.mx.QPS()`).

Imprecisions found — none load-bearing, so they do not move the verdict: (a) the disk half is NOT permanent: audit.go:88-106 cleanupLoop deletes CallLog rows older than AuditRetentionDays (default 90, settings.go:17/31) hourly, and an admin can disable call audit entirely (settings.go:25); so 'cannot be mitigated by configuration' holds only for the memory half, which has no bound or config at all. Ironically disabling call audit removes the only natural brake on request rate and accelerates the memory leak. (b) Under DB_TYPE=mysql/postgres, size:64 becomes VARCHAR(64) and an oversized row insert fails, being logged and dropped at audit.go:67-69, so the megabyte-indexed-row consequence is SQLite-default-specific; mt.stats growth is dialect-independent. (c) slb.go:213-217 (`delete(cw, pid)`) prunes the inner provider-cursor map of an existing alias, not the outer bl.rr alias keys — still a correct 'the house pattern exists' precedent, and bl.rr keys are config-derived so they are not attacker-influenced. (d) '960-byte ModelStat' is the two [60]int64 arrays; the struct is 968 B plus map bucket and the attacker-length key string. (e) The PoC must send `"messages":[]` on /v1/chat/completions: with messages absent, adapter.go:136-138 fails the parse (raw.Messages is json.RawMessage) -> 400, and ap.alias is never assigned (Observe would get ""). As filed it is correct, and /v1/messages is even cheaper since Messages is a plain slice (adapter.go:302-305), so `{"model":"x"}` alone reaches the 404.

Severity: high is correct and, if anything, conservative. Attacker lacks nothing they would not normally have (any gateway consumer holds an sk- key; the key does not need model permissions or quota headroom), the effect is irreversible for process lifetime, terminates the whole single-process server (gateway + admin API + SPA) via OOM, and per-request cost is microseconds on the reject path. It is not critical: it needs one valid API key (gateway auth is the only gate, gateway.go:215-221) and yields exhaustion, not RCE/authz-bypass/data-exfil.

Line refinement: cited line 60 is the map read; the permanent insertion is line 63 `mt.stats[model] = s`, hence corrected_line=63. The quoted block 60-64 is verbatim correct, so this is a precision refinement, not a defect in the evidence.
exploit_sketch:
Prerequisite: one valid enabled gateway API key (any tenant key; no model allowlist or quota headroom required, since the 404 short-circuits both checks).

Step 1 — mint unbounded map keys, unthrottled:
  for i in $(seq 1 200000); do
    curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST http://target:8080/v1/chat/completions \
      -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-<valid>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{"model":"zz-'$i'","messages":[]}'
  done
Each request resolves nothing (gateway.go:335/351 miss), returns 404 at 356-361 — before the allowlist (370), limiter (410) and quota (419) — and the defer at 314-319 calls Observe with the literal name, permanently adding ~968 B + key string to mt.stats (metrics.go:60-64). 200k entries ~ 300 MB plus per-row call_logs writes (gateway.go:273, model.go:253).

Step 2 — fast memory variant (length is unbounded, so count need not be large):
  send N distinct requests whose model field is a unique ~16 MiB string (cap at gateway.go:322 `io.LimitReader(c.Request.Body, 16<<20)`); ~64 such requests permanently retain ~1 GiB. Nothing evicts them; only a process restart recovers.

Step 3 — convert the attacker-chosen key count into an unauthenticated gateway-wide stall:
  while :; do curl -s http://target:8080/metrics > /dev/null; done   # no JWT (routes.go:21-24)
Each scrape runs QPS() holding mt.mu across all N entries (metrics.go:89-100, reached via admin/prom.go:15 under promMu at prom.go:113), so every legitimate gateway request blocks in Observe at gateway.go:318; the /metrics body also grows without bound (prom.go:135-139) and the admin /status payload does too (dashboard.go:137). Result: memory exhaustion (OOM of the single process serving gateway + admin + SPA), SQLite/index growth bounded only by AuditRetentionDays, and unauthenticated latency amplification keyed off attacker-chosen N.
